conviction_note: The two things I found that are genuinely not in the price point opposite ways and very nearly cancel: KBH's Q3 net-order line has an ~8% YoY community-count tailwind and a 5pp better cancellation rate that the market did not adjust for when it marked KBH down 12.6% on Lennar's -9% order print, while the standing FY2026 guide arithmetically back-loads a Q4 housing gross margin of ~17-18% against Lennar guiding its own Q4 margin FLAT at 15.5-16.0% for the identical calendar quarter. This name's reaction function is dominated by the guide, not the quarter - it rose 16.65% in June on an EPS MISS purely because the second-half guide beat fear, and fell 8.54% in December 2025 when the guide did not - so the guidance negative has veto power over the reported-quarter positives; I have shrunk it from -3.0 to -2.4 for the 8.89 days-to-cover short base per lesson 7 rather than carrying the squeeze as a separate positive finding, which would have double-counted it. I emit +0.5, at the sum and far inside the 6.48% implied move, because my net sign AGREES with both the -2.4 skew (calls bid) and the free control (-run_up_20d = +12.6), which is the definition of already being in the price; an honest near-zero is the result here and I am not manufacturing an edge on top of a name whose cheapness, short base and book discount are visible to everyone.
bar: Company guide, KB Home Q2 2026 8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2026-06-23: Q3 housing revenues $1.20-1.35bn, deliveries 2,600-2,800, housing gross margin 16.0-16.6%, SG&A 11.3-11.9%, ending communities 270-280 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/795266/000079526626000060/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm). Street bar corroborated by two agreeing sources: ~$0.89 EPS / ~$1.30bn revenue (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/earnings-preview-kb-home-kbh-140003449.html) and $0.90 EPS (https://news.alphastreet.com/kb-home-kbh-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-0-90-reports-september-22/). Note the $1.30bn street revenue sits at the TOP of the company's own $1.20-1.35bn housing-revenue range, so the bar is harder than the guide midpoint, which is why I size the beat at only +0.5%.
positioning_check: 7.54m shares short = 12.91% of float, 12.31% of shares outstanding, 8.89 days to cover; prior month 7.56m, i.e. essentially FLAT - shorts did not build into this print, they are a standing position (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/kbh/statistics/, read 2026-09-22). Baseline skew_25d_vol_points is -2.4, i.e. NEGATIVE: the option market is paying more for upside than downside, corroborated by a put/call open interest ratio of 0.62. Stock at 0.77x book ($61.93 BVPS at 31 May 2026, per the 10-Q) with $775m remaining of a $1bn authorisation. So skew, run-up (-12.6%) and valuation all lean the same way - long - which is precisely why I am NOT sizing a long here: every visible signal already says it, and my job is to beat the baseline, not to restate it. The flat month-on-month short interest is the one thing that mildly weakens the squeeze story and it is recorded here rather than left out.

findings.finding: KB Home goes into this print with average community count up roughly 8% YoY (Q3-2025 average 259 / ending 264; Q2-2026 average 278 up 9%, Q3-2026 ending guided 270-280) and a cancellation rate of 12% of gross orders against 17% in the year-ago Q3 - so its net-order line has two mechanical tailwinds that Lennar, whose -9% order print is what the market marked KBH down on, does not have.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net orders is the one line in the release that is not guided, so it is where a genuine surprise can sit. On 2026-06-23 KBH printed net orders of 3,317 (-4% YoY) against a sector reading far worse and rose 16.65% the next session despite missing EPS $0.43 vs $0.45; on 2025-09-24 net orders of 2,950 (-4%) landed in line and the stock moved -0.63%. The line pays when it separates KBH from the sector read and is ignored when it tracks it.
findings.why_not_priced: KBH fell 12.6% over 20 sessions and roughly tracked Lennar's post-print de-rating. If the market had done this arithmetic it would not have applied Lennar's -9% pace decline one-for-one to a company carrying ~8% more selling communities and 5 percentage points fewer cancellations: at Q3-2025's 3.8 monthly absorption per community KBH needs only 3.4 (a -11% pace decline, worse than Lennar's) on 280 communities to print net orders down just 3% YoY. Every published preview frames tonight as 'will orders hold' in the abstract and none of them carries the community base. Net of the rest of the company: deliveries and margin are both inside the company's own June guide and therefore cannot surprise much either way, so this line is not being offset by a hidden negative elsewhere in the release - the offset is the forward guide, which I size separately and negatively below.
findings.independence: The community-count and cancellation figures come from two DIFFERENT KB Home releases (Q3-2025 8-K of 2025-09-24 above and the Q2-2026 8-K of 2026-06-23, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/795266/000079526626000060/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm), so this is not one document read twice. Pointing the same way from an unrelated source: Hovnanian, reporting the quarter ended 31 July 2026, said sales pace stayed 'resilient, with contracts per community above historical averages' while total contracts fell - i.e. the sector's order decline is a community/pace composition effect, which is the variable KBH is long of (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/20/3348449/12793/en/hovnanian-enterprises-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results.html).
findings._note: The Q2-2026 release is shared with finding 2 below; see that finding's independence field.

findings.finding: The Q3 delivery guide of 2,600-2,800 homes implies only 57-62% conversion of the 4,526-home backlog KBH carried into the quarter, against 66.5% actually converted in Q2-2026 (2,395 delivered from an opening backlog of 3,604) and ~71% in Q3-2025 (3,393 from ~4,764) - so the revenue guide carries a conversion cushion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deliveries landing inside the guided range has not moved this stock in either direction: 2025-09-24 deliveries 3,393 (in range), move -0.63%; 2026-03-24 deliveries 2,370, move -1.55%. The two large moves in the baseline (+16.65%, -8.54%) both came off the forward guide, not the delivery line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is arithmetic off two primary documents that no aggregator publishes - the opening backlog is derived (4,526 ending + 2,395 delivered - 3,317 net orders = 3,604 opening), and the conversion series is not in any preview. But I size it small and say why: this outcome lands INSIDE what the company guided on 23 June, so the market has already been told to expect it, and the conversion rate legitimately falls as the built-to-order mix lengthens cycle times. The honest read is that it lowers the probability of a delivery MISS rather than creating a beat, and the +0.5 reflects exactly that and nothing more.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2-2026 8-K with finding 1 - counted once between them, which is why this one is sized at +0.5 rather than at the standalone value of a conversion cushion. The 71% Q3-2025 comparator comes from a different document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/795266/000079526625000092/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm).

findings.finding: Two peer builders printed sequential gross-margin IMPROVEMENT in windows that overlap KBH's June-August quarter and that both landed after KBH last spoke on 23 June: Lennar's Q3 (identical 31 August quarter end) went 15.3% to 15.8% with incentives moderating to 12%, and Hovnanian's quarter ended 31 July was its SECOND consecutive sequential gross-margin improvement - which is the same shape as KBH's guided step from 15.2% to 16.0-16.6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Housing gross margin landing inside the guided range has not been a mover for KBH; on 2026-06-23 the reported 15.2% was a four-point YoY collapse and the stock rose 16.65% anyway because the forward margin guide was the story. The margin line pays only via the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The wire framing of Lennar was 'double miss, guidance cut, 52-week low' and of the margin line specifically 'down from 17.5% a year ago'. The SEQUENTIAL direction - up 50bp with incentives falling - is the reading that bears on KBH's guided step and it is not what the headlines carried, and Hovnanian's 20 August print is barely covered at all. Sized small deliberately: KBH's 16.0-16.6% is a guided number, so confirming it only removes downside rather than creating upside, and the step KBH needs (80-140bp) is larger than the 50bp Lennar achieved. If the market had fully priced a confirmed margin step, KBH would not have de-rated in lockstep with LEN over the last 20 sessions.
findings.independence: Two separate issuers' own releases, filed 27 days apart, neither of which shares a document with any other finding here. Hovnanian: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/20/3348449/12793/en/hovnanian-enterprises-reports-fiscal-2026-third-quarter-results.html

findings.finding: KBH's standing FY2026 guide ($4.90-5.30bn housing revenue, 16.1-16.5% housing gross margin, 10,500-11,000 deliveries) arithmetically back-loads a Q4 that needs roughly $1.45-1.85bn of housing revenue - flat to -13% YoY after quarters down 23%, 27% and ~20% - at an IMPLIED Q4 housing gross margin of about 17-18%, while Lennar has just guided its own Q4 (same calendar quarter) to a FLAT 15.5-16.0% and said the incentive cost of rate buydowns is the emerging pressure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the ONLY line that has moved this stock. 2026-06-23: EPS missed and the stock rose 16.65% because the second-half guide (Q3 margin 16.0-16.6%, FY 10,500-11,000 deliveries) beat fear. 2025-12-18: -8.54% on a disappointing forward guide. 2025-03-24: -5.21%. Five of the baseline's seven reactions are negative and the two positives were both guide-driven. A trim to this FY range tonight lands squarely on the line with the largest historical response.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY range itself is wire copy; the implied Q4 decomposition is not, and no preview I could find states it. Derived from primary documents only: Q1 housing revenue 2,370 x $452,100 = $1.071bn at 15.3%, Q2 2,395 x $461,900 = $1.106bn at 15.2%, Q3 guided $1.275bn midpoint at 16.3% - which leaves roughly $291m of gross profit on ~$1.65bn of Q4 revenue, i.e. ~17.6%. If the market had priced a guide cut, KBH would not be trading 8.0% ABOVE its 52-week low while Lennar made a NEW 52-week low on its own print six days ago; that gap is the part of this that is unmarked. Shrunk from a standalone -3.0 to -2.4 per the crowded-short rule: 12.91% of float and 8.89 days to cover is a squeeze mechanism in its own right, and this exact setup produced +16.65% on a worse EPS number in June.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2-2026 8-K with findings 1 and 2, but reads a different object from each (the forward FY range, not the community count or the backlog), and it is signed the opposite way - so it cannot be the same fact counted twice. The independent corroboration is Lennar's own Q4 guidance, from a different issuer's call: deliveries 22,000-23,000, new orders 19,500-20,500 (below its own just-printed 20,879), gross margin 15.5-16.0% (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/09/17/lennar-len-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). I am deliberately NOT resting this on the 16 September Fed hike or the 4.96% 10-year: macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a counterparty says it, and Lennar is the counterparty that said it.

findings.finding: KB Home will deliver this print and set its FY guide with no permanent CFO: Robert Dillard resigned effective 8 May 2026 with no successor disclosed in the 8-K, and none has been announced in the four and a half months since - under a CEO, Robert McGibney, who only took the seat on 1 March 2026 and is in his second full quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct precedent in the baseline's seven prints - the CFO seat was vacant for the first time at the 2026-06-23 print, which was +16.65%, so this has NOT yet been a negative for this stock. That is the main reason it is sized at half a point rather than more.
findings.why_not_priced: The resignation itself was an April news item and is stale; what is not priced is the DURATION - a $3.0bn builder giving its most important guide of the year in its fourth month without a permanent CFO. A new CEO plus an interim finance chief is the standard setup for resetting an outlook rather than defending it, and it lowers the odds of a bold capital-return announcement that would otherwise be the obvious offset at 0.77x book with $775m of authorisation live. If this were priced there would be a preview naming it; none of the four previews I read mentions the CFO seat. I size it small and label the inference as inference: the 8-K is a document, the behavioural conclusion from it is not.
findings.independence: None - this rests on one 8-K and no other source points the same way. Recorded as 'none' rather than dressed up, and sized accordingly.

outside_window.finding: The Census/HUD August 2026 New Residential Sales release is scheduled for 24 September 2026 - two days after this print and one day after the exit - and July already printed 607,000 SAAR, down 10.5% month-on-month, with 488,000 new homes for sale. It is the cleanest read on whether KBH's Q4 order assumption is achievable and the trade will never see it.

searched_and_found_nothing: KB Home investor relations news-release page (https://investor.kbhome.com/company-news/news-releases/default.aspx) returned navigation only, no listing - could not confirm or exclude any company release between 23 June and today from this surface

KBH's own advertised incentive page https://www.kbhome.com/special-rate2 returned HTTP 404, so I could not read the current buydown rate off the company's own pricing page; a San Diego community page advertising 5.875% (6.886% APR) was the only live datapoint and is one community, not a policy

No new share-repurchase authorisation since the $1bn of 27 October 2025; $775m remained at 31 May 2026 with $75m bought in Q2 at ~$53.57 average

Inventory-impairment risk: KBH's Q2 charges were immaterial ($3.1m impairment on one community, $2.5m of land-option abandonments) and I found no peer taking a large August-quarter land charge, so I could not build a sourced impairment finding and did not manufacture one
KBH hiring pages, app-store/customer-forum sentiment and division-level job postings - no retrievable signal that separates KBH from the sector
baseline_tension: My net sign AGREES with the -2.4 skew (calls bid, put/call OI 0.62) and with the free control (-run_up_20d = +12.6), which by this stage's own standard means it is already in the price - so the honest answer is a near-zero, not a long; the one thing I found that cuts against all three of them is the stretched implied Q4 margin in the standing FY guide, and it is the only reason my number is not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (a finding inside the guided range is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect) cut two findings hard: the backlog-conversion cushion from +1.2 to +0.5 and the peer margin confirmation from +1.0 to +0.6, because deliveries of 2,600-2,800 and a 16.0-16.6% margin are both things KB Home guided to on 23 June. Only the net-order finding survives at size, because KBH does not guide net orders.

Lesson 7 (positioning is the thing to beat, not colour) DROPPED my sixth finding entirely - a +1.0 'crowded short plus 0.77x book plus calls bid' long - because that is the -2.4 skew restated, and the skew is in the sealed baseline. The squeeze was re-expressed the way the lesson prescribes: as a shrink to the negative, taking the guidance finding from -3.0 to -2.4, so the mechanism is counted once instead of twice.

Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until a counterparty says it) re-anchored the guidance finding: I had built it partly on the 16 September Fed hike and the 4.96% 10-year. Those are now explicitly excluded and the finding rests on KBH's own guide arithmetic plus Lennar's stated Q4 margin guide of 15.5-16.0%, which is the direct counterparty speaking.

Lesson 6's bar rule checked out rather than capping me: the bar is sourceable to a company guide AND to two agreeing estimate sources, so no size cap applies - but it also revealed the $1.30bn street revenue sits at the TOP of the $1.20-1.35bn company range, which pulled print_vs_bar_pct from +1.0 to +0.5.
Lesson 9 (size a segment finding net of the rest) added the explicit net-of line to the net-order finding and trimmed it 2.5 to 2.2.

Lesson 3 (your caveat has to reach the number) is why expected_move_pct is +0.5 rather than the +2.0 I drafted: baseline_tension says my positives agree with the skew and the run-up, so the emitted number sits at the sum of the findings and not above it.

Lesson 8 (understatement is the systematic error) was considered and deliberately NOT applied - it governs thin-coverage names with a confirmed unpriced number, and KBH carries roughly fifteen estimates and a $58.42 average target, so it does not reach here.
Net effect: impact sum +1.9 to +0.4, expected move +2.0 to +0.5, findings 6 to 5. The file made this name materially smaller and it was right to.
